pr_body:
This let's systemd-repart respect the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable when creating directories in the local tree through `MakeDirectories` or `CopyFiles`.

To do this, it does two things:
- When a directory is created in `mkdir_p_root`, it set's timestamps (`mtime` and `atime`) for the directory that's being created. Additionally, it will fixup the `mtime` for the directory things are copied *into*, if `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set. Otherwise, times are left untouched (`UTIME_OMIT`). The fixup of the upper directory is necessary, as otherwise, when creating a directory in it, it's `mtime` would change.
- For the reason mentioned above, we also need to fixup the `mtime` of the upper directory if we copy a file into it.

The changes can be verified with https://github.com/msanft/systemd-repart-repro-bug.

Fixes #32117.

issue_context.title: systemd-repart does not respect `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` when creating directories in the temporary local OS tree
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

255

### Used distribution

NixOS 24.05

### Linux kernel version used

6.8.2

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-repart

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

systemd-repart should respect the [`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/1eeae735ad3d42d60f6513dea6d9ab0d2d858e82/docs/ENVIRONMENT.md?plain=1#L398) environment variable when [creating files / directories](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/1eeae735ad3d42d60f6513dea6d9ab0d2d858e82/src/shared/copy.c#L1020) in the local OS tree through `xopenat_lock_full` with `O_CREAT`, as it happens here when [populating the local temporary tree](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/1eeae735ad3d42d60f6513dea6d9ab0d2d858e82/src/partition/repart.c#L4859).

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

systemd-repart creates the directories / files in the temporary local OS tree with undeterministic timestamps (i.e. `atime` and `mtime`), causing irreproducible image builds.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

I've created a repository with a minimal reproduction example here:

https://github.com/msanft/systemd-repart-repro-bug

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_

review_comments: `!timestamp_is_set(ts)` ? I mean, we should also ignore `ts == 0`. Or does this intentionally accept `ts == 0`?

[Many tools](https://github.com/search?q=SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH%3D0&type=code), namely NixOS, for which reproducible builds are especially important, set the variable to 0. The specification of `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` also permits setting it to 0, which is why I think it should be supported here, too, if you don't have any objections.
But setting 0 timestamp sounds spurious for me... Or `futimens()` handles 0 gracefully?

Yes, `futimens()` handles it. It sets the timestamps to 0 like so: 

```
  File: /var/tmp/.#repartc9a185024a9ea6f2/somedir
  Size: 4096      	Blocks: 8          IO Block: 4096   directory
Device: fd00h/64768d	Inode: 6686698     Links: 2
Access: (0755/drwxr-xr-x)  Uid: ( 1001/      ms)   Gid: ( 1001/      ms)
Access: 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000000 +0000
Modify: 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000000 +0000
```
OK. Still I want to filter out 0, but not a strong opinion. Feel free to ignore this.
this call should not be done if the source epch stuff is not used.
this will fall apart if uid or gid are specified but no timestamp, because nfd will not be initialized then.

this commit should really be merged with the one using this function.

We want "perfect" commits after all, i.e. that make sense of their own, and work on their own. But if this commit is merged alone then the compiler will be unhappy because it generally dislikes static functions that are not used by anything.

doesn't matter much but i think we should probably debug log if the overflow condition.

a simple way would be to simply do `r = -ERANGE` here, and then change the `else if (r != -ENXIO)`  to just `if (r != -ENXIO)`
This is not necessary when uid, gid, and ts are unspecified. Please conditionalize.
Just return early here if `ts == USEC_INFINITY && !uid_is_valid(uid) && !gid_is_valid(gid)`? Then, move declaration of `nfd` below so that it's more obvious when it would be used.
